title: Deterministic recommendation apply + replayable webhook contract
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Provide a deterministic, replayable API and webhook contract for applying batching/caching recommendations from Redwood Optimize such that downstream callers (Console, Dedicated controllers, and external automation agents) can safely issue retries, perform rollbacks, and reconcile state without risk of duplicated changes or partial failures.

Scope: define HTTP endpoints, idempotency semantics, minimal event payloads, webhook acknowledgement/checkpoint protocol, SDK helpers, server-side conflict resolution rules, and a canary rollout plan. This ticket focuses on the API contract and server behavior; implementation tasks are split into follow-ups for SDKs, control-plane agent, and e2e tests.

Key design constraints and non-goals:
- Must work across hosted and Dedicated/private control planes where network reliability varies.
- Should avoid long-lived per-apply locks that block throughput; prefer sequence/checkpointing.
- Non-goal: implement automatic change reversal logic beyond a deterministic rollback API (we provide hooks and markers for policy-enforced automatic rollbacks in a follow-up).

Proposed API endpoints and semantics:
1) POST /v1/optimize/apply
   - Purpose: submit a batched recommendation bundle for apply.
   - Required headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>, Idempotency-Key: <client-idempotency-token> (recommended), X-Apply-Source: <source> (console|sdk|automation)
   - Body fields (minimal): apply_id (client-generated UUID/string), recommendations: [ { rec_id, target_path, patch, expected_version? } ], metadata: { workload, model, estimate_cost_savings }
   - Behavior: Server treats apply_id as the canonical idempotency key. If an apply_id has been processed, server returns previous outcome (200 with status or 409 with conflict details). Server validates expected_version if present and fails fast with 409 on mismatch.

2) POST /v1/optimize/apply/{apply_id}/commit
   - Purpose: finalize and start asynchronous commit (if apply endpoint accepted but did not execute atomically).
   - Returns: 202 Accepted with a commit_token used for status polling.

3) GET /v1/optimize/apply/{apply_id}/status
   - Purpose: query deterministic outcome (applied | rolled_back | partial | failed). Responses include sequence_number and server_checkpoint_token for use in webhooks.

4) Webhook: POST to registered callback URL(s) when an apply progresses states (queued -> applying -> applied | failed).
   - Webhook payload includes: apply_id, sequence_number (monotonic per-apply), event_type, timestamp, server_checkpoint_token (opaque string), delta_summary, and an idempotency_token for that event.
   - Receiver semantics: Recipients MUST respond 2xx to acknowledge; server will retry on 5xx or network failure. Acking the webhook does NOT imply the recipient has applied anything locally — it only acknowledges delivery.

Replayable webhook contract and checkpointing:
- Each webhook includes a server_checkpoint_token that encodes the last durable position for that apply (opaque to clients). The receiver may request events since a checkpoint by calling GET /v1/optimize/apply/{apply_id}/events?since_checkpoint=<token>. This enables receivers that were down to replay missing events deterministically.
- Server retains events for replay for 30 days by default; retention is configurable per-customer in Dedicated.

Idempotency and conflict resolution rules:
- apply_id is primary idempotency key (server-enforced). If a client uses Idempotency-Key header and does not provide apply_id, server maps header->apply_id for a TTL of 24 hours.
- When two distinct apply requests touch overlapping resources, server computes a deterministic merge/ordering using per-resource sequence numbers. If non-commutative changes are detected, server rejects later applies with a 409 and includes a conflict report and suggested pre-apply reconciliation steps.
- Expected_version in a recommendation entry is honored as a precondition; mismatches cause fail-fast 409 and include latest_version in response.

SDK helpers and recommended client behavior:
- SDKs expose an ApplyClient that handles apply_id generation, Idempotency-Key header injection, exponential backoff for transient failures, and automatic GET status polling with backoff.
- SDKs will surface server checkpoint tokens and provide convenience methods to replay webhook events via the events endpoint.
- Clients should avoid unchecked retries beyond a TTL (default 24h) and should rely on server responses for finality.

Observability and telemetry:
- Emit events: apply_submitted, apply_conflict, apply_committed, apply_rolled_back, websocket_replay_attempt, webhook_dropped. All events include apply_id and sequence_number.
- Dashboard: new Optimize > Automation > Apply Log with filters by customer, apply_id, status, and rec_id. Link: https://dashboard.redwood.ai/optimize/apply-log (placeholder).

Rollback story:
- Rollbacks are explicit: POST /v1/optimize/apply/{apply_id}/rollback with reason and optional force flag. Server returns 202 and emits webhook events for rollback steps. Rollback is deterministic and written to the apply history so any replay of events includes the rollback.

Failure modes and DLQ policy:
- If webhook delivery repeatedly fails, server routes events to customer-configured webhook DLQ (SQS/Kafka) and emits an alert. For hosted customers without DLQ configured, events are persisted and retried for 30 days; after expiry an audit record is created and a notification is sent to account admins.

Security and compliance considerations:
- Webhook payloads are signed using per-customer HMAC keys. Receivers must verify signatures. Signing metadata included as headers: X-RW-Signature and X-RW-Key-Id.
- Checkpoint tokens are opaque and have no PII. Audit logs record full apply payloads for 90 days (configurable).

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Implement server endpoints behind feature-flag; provide backwards-compatible response shapes.
2) Ship SDK v0.12 with ApplyClient helpers.
3) Enable for internal Redwood Optimize teams and run a 2-week canary with opt-in customers.
4) Gradually enable auto-replay and DLQ features; monitor apply_conflict rates and webhook delivery success >99.5%.

Open questions and trade-offs considered:
- Stateful vs stateless: we chose lightweight per-apply state + event log to allow replay without heavy locks. Heavy locks were rejected to avoid throughput regressions.
- Retention window size: default 30 days for hosted; Dedicated customers may request longer retention.
- Rollback atomicity: true atomic rollback across multiple resources is expensive; we provide deterministic rollback steps and idempotent markers so agents can reconcile without global locks.

Next steps (actionable):
- Finalize JSON schema for webhook and events (follow-up PR).
- Add server-side unit tests for idempotency and conflict scenarios.
- Draft SDK design doc and example integration in Console automation (linked below).
